name: Vitamin A (Retinol)
summary: A fat-soluble vitamin essential for the visual cycle (rhodopsin), epithelial differentiation, immune function and embryonic development.

conditions.label: Deficiency
conditions.description: A leading cause of preventable childhood blindness worldwide; impairs the retinal visual cycle and epithelial integrity.

affects.effect: Night blindness, xerophthalmia, Bitot spots, keratomalacia
affects.detail: Reduced rhodopsin regeneration causes night blindness first; progressive conjunctival/corneal drying (xerophthalmia) can end in corneal melting (keratomalacia) and irreversible blindness.

ageModifiers.child: Young children are most vulnerable; vitamin A deficiency is a major cause of preventable childhood blindness and raises measles mortality.

affects.detail: Loss of epithelial differentiation causes rough, dry skin with keratin plugs around follicles.

affects.effect: Impaired mucosal immunity, more respiratory infection
affects.detail: Compromised epithelial barriers and immune function increase susceptibility to respiratory and gastrointestinal infection.

references.title: Vitamin A and Carotenoids — Health Professional Fact Sheet

conditions.label: Toxicity (hypervitaminosis A)
conditions.description: Excess preformed retinol is hepatotoxic and teratogenic.

affects.detail: Chronic excess accumulates in hepatic stellate cells, driving fibrosis and portal hypertension.
Acute excess can raise intracranial pressure, causing headache, blurred vision and, in infants, a bulging fontanelle.
High-dose retinoids in early pregnancy cause craniofacial, cardiac and CNS birth defects.

genderModifiers.female: In people who are or may become pregnant, high-dose vitamin A / retinoids are strongly teratogenic and must be avoided.
